package_info.why_malicious: The injected code is designed to steal payment card data from e-commerce customers by intercepting and exfiltrating sensitive information during the checkout process. The code is loaded from an external, attacker-controlled domain and operates without user consent, violating the integrity and security of the affected websites.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the checkout page is loaded by the customer
execution_context.file_location: Injected into Magento 1 checkout page templates (e.g., app/design/frontend/base/default/template/checkout/onepage.phtml or similar)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects a remote JavaScript file from an attacker-controlled domain into the checkout page, allowing the external script to execute in the customer's browser, access the DOM, and perform unauthorized actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading JavaScript from an unrelated, external domain on a payment page is highly suspicious, especially when the domain is not associated with the e-commerce site and is not a known third-party provider.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout pages should only load scripts from trusted, first-party or vetted third-party sources. Injecting scripts from unknown domains is not expected and introduces significant risk.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate analytics or payment providers load scripts from external domains, but these are well-known, documented, and subject to security review.
key_indicators: Script tag referencing an attacker-controlled domain in sensitive checkout templates
Script loaded from a domain not associated with the business or known providers
Modification of core checkout template files to include unauthorized external scripts

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the checkout form is submitted by the customer
execution_context.file_location: Loaded from https://naturalfreshmall.com/xxx.js, executed in the customer's browser

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon checkout form submission, the code hooks the form event, programmatically collects payment card details from the DOM, and sends the sensitive data via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled external server, resulting in exfiltration of customer payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating payment card data to an external server is a classic sign of a payment skimmer and constitutes a severe breach of payment security standards.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Payment data should only be transmitted to the legitimate payment processor's secure endpoint, never to unknown or unauthorized third-party domains. There should be no interception or duplication of sensitive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors may collect card data, but only to their own secure endpoints, with user consent, and in compliance with PCI DSS requirements.
key_indicators: Direct access to payment card input fields in the DOM
JavaScript event listener on the checkout form submission
Outbound POST requests containing card data to an untrusted external domain
No user notification or consent for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to Magento 1 store via SQL injection, PHP object injection, or exploitation of known vulnerabilities.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify website files and inject malicious code.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script tag is injected into checkout page templates to load external JavaScript from an attacker-controlled domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of attacker-controlled JavaScript in customer browsers during checkout.

attack_chain.action: External JavaScript hooks into the checkout form, collects payment card data from the DOM, and exfiltrates it to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Theft of customer payment information (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Checkout page loading JavaScript from untrusted or newly registered external domains
JavaScript code accessing payment form fields and sending data to external servers during checkout
Unexpected modification of checkout page template files in Magento 1 installations
file_indicators: Unusual or unauthorized changes in app/design/frontend/*/template/checkout/*.phtml files
File integrity mismatches or unauthorized modifications in core template files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS requests to naturalfreshmall.com or similar attacker-controlled domains from customer browsers during checkout
POST requests containing payment card data to external domains not associated with legitimate payment processors
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized script tags referencing external domains in checkout page templates, inspect network traffic from checkout pages for exfiltration of payment data to untrusted domains, and audit file integrity of Magento template files for unexpected or unauthorized modifications. Correlate file changes with network activity to identify active skimming attacks.
